top_signals.title: Equatorial Guinea Rewrites Oil Law After Production Collapses 85%
top_signals.summary: Equatorial Guinea will approve a new hydrocarbon law on Monday after crude production collapsed to just 20,000 barrels per day in September, down from roughly 140,000 bpd in 2020. The 120,000-bpd loss has reduced OPEC’s smallest producer to a fraction of its former output and contributed to an economy the International Monetary Fund expects to shrink 1.7% this year. Hydrocarbons Minister Antonio Oburu Ondo said the new law will make contractual terms more flexible and offer oil companies a wider range of structures based on their appetite…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.
